messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: non-centered parameterisation for bounded parameters
parts:
When fitting a hierarchical continuous time dynamic model, there are a number of parameters I need to keep within certain bounds. In order to estimate these parameters and maintain them within necessary bounds, I use a range of log and exp transforms, which based on readings here I suspect might be problematic? The code looks like:

##############################
parameters{
vec<lower=0.0001,upper=.9999>[nparams] hypermeans;
cholesky_factor_corr[nparams] hypercorrchol;
vector[nparams] hypersd;
vector[nparams*nsubjects] indparamsnoisebase;
}

model{
vec[nparams] lognegloghypermeans;
vector[nparams*nsubjects] indparamsnoise;

hypercorrchol~ lkj_corr_cholesky(1);
indparamsnoisebase ~ normal(0,1); 

 for(subjecti in 1:nsubjects){    // this just rolls the indparamsnoisebase vector into the appropriate shape array of individual parameter vectors
 for(parami in 1:nparams){
 indparamsnoise[subjecti][parami]<-indparamsnoisebase[(subjecti-1)*nparams+parami];
 }
 }

lognegloghypermeans <- log(-log(hypermeans));

 for(subjecti in 1:nsubjects){
      indparams[subjecti] <-  exp(-exp( lognegloghypermeans + diag_pre_multiply(hypersd,hypercorrchol) * indparamsnoise[subjecti] ))
}
#######################################

from there, I go on to construct the various matrices and calculations I need based on (mostly) linear transformations of indparams. Based on reading here, I suspect this approach may be problematic with all the logs and exps, but can't see how to ensure the hypermeans + individual elements stay within the necessary bounds otherwise. (except by specifying the distribution of the final parameters needed explicitly in centered form). I thought a logit approach might be better, but it was no faster and occasionally resulted in non-finite gradients. Is there a better way to generate non-centered parameter vectors while staying within necessary bounds? Thoughts and advice would be very welcome! Thank you.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] non-centered parameterisation for bounded parameters
parts:
Internally, we map some x in (-inf, inf) into (L, U) by:

f(x) = L + (U - L) * inv_logit(x)

But that involves exp on the inside, which is not great. The
only time you get non-finite gradients here is when exp() overflows,
which means x is outside of (-300, 300) or so.

You probably want to use eta > 1 in the lkj_corr_cholesky for
some shrinkage toward a unit correlation matrix.
If you use 1, you can just skip the sampling statement altogether
as it's just a uniform.

You should not need (0.0001, 0.9999) and should use just (0, 1).

The code you sent won't work because

vector[nparams*nsubjects] indparamsnoise;

is incompatible with

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] non-centered parameterisation for bounded parameters
parts:
But exp(-exp(x)) maps (-inf, inf) to (0, inf), not to a bounded
interval, so I don't understand the comparison to a scaled
and translated inv_logit.

For a general (-inf, inf) to (L, inf) transform, we use

f(x) = exp(x) + L

Any x > log(300), or x > 5.7 or so will underflow exp(-exp(x)),
so that doesn't give you a lot of latitude.

- Bob
